summary: Democratic Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham was term-limited, so the seat was open. Deb Haaland (Democrat) defeated Gregg Hull (Republican).

candidates.name: Deb Haaland
candidates.bio: Deb Haaland was U.S. Secretary of the Interior under President Biden. Before that she served in the U.S. House, where she was first elected in 2018.

positions.summary: Says she would raise the minimum wage and child tax credit, ban landlords from using AI algorithms to set rents, and speed up permits to build more housing.
Says she would address the doctor shortage, protect rural hospitals, ban medical debt from credit reports, and expand the Health Care Affordability Fund.
Says she would expand the Opportunity Scholarship to provide free tuition, including for graduate education, and expand community schools.
Says she would invest in more renewable energy to create jobs, lower energy costs, and make New Mexico the energy capital of the country.

candidates.name: Gregg Hull
candidates.bio: Gregg Hull was mayor of Rio Rancho from 2014 to 2026.

positions.summary: Says he would use targeted incentives to diversify the economy in areas like aerospace and advanced manufacturing, and reform occupational licensing.
Says he would tie part of school funding to gains in literacy, math and graduation rates and expand school choice and charter schools.
Says he would protect rural health systems, reform medical malpractice laws, and lower prescription drug costs.
Says he would expand the state's energy portfolio "to include all sources" while "unleashing our oil and gas operations."

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (MultiState governors tracker, updated Nov 4, 35 of 36 races called) Summary originally noted that figures reflected about 95% counted. Certified: the New Mexico State Canvassing Board certified the results on Nov. 24, 2026 (Secretary of State release). Shares are computed from the Secretary of State page labeled Official Results.
